newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-TENDULKAR DECLARATION GIVES INDIA CHANCE OF VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULKAR DECLARATION GIVES INDIA CHANCE OF VICTORY.

text.p: An enterprising declaration by Indian captain Sachin Tendulkar gave his side an outside chance of a morale-boosting win on the fourth day of the third and final test against South Africa on Sunday.
Leading by 89 on the first innings at the Wanderers, the Indian batsmen took their second innings to 266 for eight before Tendulkar called them in and set South Africa 356 to win from 95 overs.

The declaration allowed Tendulkar five overs at the South African openers and he was rewarded when Andrew Hudson played around the penultimate ball of the day and was bowled by leg-spinner Anil Kumble for three.
At the close South Africa were four for one.

With a full day to bowl on Monday, India, who were well beaten in the first two tests, will fancy their chances of a consolation win although on a similarly placid pitch last year, England captain Mike Atherton made 185 not out on the last day to defy South Africa.

First innings centurion Rahul Dravid again top-scored for the tourists, this time with 81. When he lost his wicket to be eighth out Tendulkar chose to declare rather than watch Doda Ganesh and Venkatesh Prasad struggle against the home team attack.
India began the day slowly and scored just 72 runs in the morning session. But, having built a sound foundation, their batsmen then took the attack to South Africa.
Nayan Mongia set the tone with 50 from 89 balls and his opening partner Vikram Rathore made a test best 44.

Tendulkar failed, making only nine before he fell to South African captain and part-time bowler Hansie Cronje for the second time in the game, but Dravid and Saurav Ganguly added 108 for the fourth wicket to freeze South Africa out.

Ganguly eventually fell to the wiles of left-arm wrist-spinner Paul Adams who turned the ball massively between the left-hander's bat and pad to bowl him for an enterprising 60 made from 93 balls with 11 fours and a six.
South African all-rounder Shaun Pollock trapped Mohammad Azharuddin lbw for two but may have incurred the wrath of ICC match referee Barry Jarman.
Pollock appeared to send Azharuddin on his way with a torrent of verbal abuse and the former Indian captain was visibly upset as he left the field.
Dravid made a controlled 81 made from 146 balls with 11 boundaries before he finally fell, sweeping Adams straight to Daryll Cullinan at square-leg.
Adams finished with three for 80 and gave good support to Donald who took three for 38 in 18 overs of high-speed bowling.

Donald's counterparts in the Indian team, pacemen Javagal Srinath and Prasad, may hold the key to the result. But with few balls misbehaving for either seamers or spinners the odds are still heavily in favour of a draw.
